slides.text:
A variable gives a name to a value. In Rust a variable is **immutable by default**: once it has a value, it cannot be changed unless you ask for it.

In this module you create variables, make them changeable with `mut`, copy values between them and handle the ones you do not use.

`let` creates a variable. A plain one keeps its first value for good. Add `mut` and it can be assigned again.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
slides.code:
let name = value
    name stays the same

let mut name = value
    name = another value

exercises.title: Your first variables
exercises.guide: Create three variables with `let` and print them.

chunks.guide: `let` gives a name to a value. Names are written in lowercase, with underscores between words.

notes.text: Makes a variable and gives it a value.

chunks.guide: Print all three variables. Each `{}` takes the next value, in order.
chunks.text: println!("lives {}, level {}, coins {}", max_lives, level, coins);

exercises.title: A variable that changes
exercises.guide: Declare a variable with `mut`, then assign it a new value.

chunks.guide: Write `mut` after `let` to allow the value to change later.

notes.text: Lets this variable be assigned again.

chunks.guide: Assign a new value with `=`. Do not write `let` again: it is the same variable.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: `attempts` is assigned twice. Follow each step, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: The first `println!` runs before any reassignment, so it shows 1. The last assignment wins, so the second shows 3.

exercises.title: Only what changes
exercises.guide: Each variable decides for itself: only the one that changes gets `mut`.

chunks.guide: `speed` will change, `limit` will not. Only `speed` is `mut`.
Change `speed`. Assigning to `limit` would be an error.

exercises.title: Copy a value
exercises.guide: Initialize a variable from another one. The copy keeps its own value.

notes.text: Copies the number into the new variable.

chunks.text:
let mut stock = 8;
    let saved = stock;

exercises.title: Change the original
exercises.guide: The program must print `30 80`. Fill in the two names.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Follow each assignment, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `best = latest` copies the value of `latest` into `best`, so both hold 14.

exercises.title: Print a receipt
exercises.guide: Build a small receipt: values that are used, one that is not, and one given later.

chunks.guide: `_note` is never printed. The underscore tells the compiler that is on purpose.

notes.text: The leading underscore stops the unused warning.

chunks.guide: Declare `paid` now and give it its value on the next line.
